html:
The Kashaya are a Pomo people of the Sonoma coast in Northern California, living between the Gualala and Russian rivers. They spoke Kashaya, one of the seven Pomoan languages of the Pomo.

They lived on the coast and in the redwood hills, fishing, gathering acorns and seaweed and making fine baskets. In 1812 the Russian American Company built Fort Ross on their land, the southern outpost of Russian America, and many Kashaya worked there until the Russians left in 1841. Their neighbours were the Southern Pomo inland and the Coast Miwok to the south. In the 1900s the Kashaya kept their religion alive through the Bole Maru dream dances, led by the prophet Essie Parrish.
